newsitem.title: USA: Reputed U.S. gambling ring smashed, 59 arrested.
newsitem.headline: Reputed U.S. gambling ring smashed, 59 arrested.

text.p: Dozens of people linked to the Luchese organised crime family have been charged with running an illegal $1 billion-a-year sports gambling ring, officials said Friday.
The arrests of 59 people were the result of a six-month joint investigation by authorities in New York and New Jersey.
The sophisticated interstate betting system was believed to be a $1 billion-a-year operation, said New York state Attorney General Dennis Vacco.
At one location alone, the suspects did $10 million worth of illegal business in 10 weeks, he said. They were connected to the Luchese organised crime family, he added.
The raid was particularly satisfying because it came amid the NCAA college basketball tournament, Vacco said.
"We are right now in the heart of the sports gambling season, ... a very lucrative time of year for them," Vacco said.
The ring used a sophisticated computer system to help gamblers get up-to-the-minute betting odds from Las Vegas, he said.
The suspects face a variety of charges including promoting gambling and conspiracy and, if convicted, face up to seven years in prison.
